ov: The first animal people domesticated, bred from wolves by hunter-gatherers more than 14,000 years ago, before farming began. There are around 450 official breeds, more than for any other mammal.

why.dg: Most dogs are harmless, but dog bites affect tens of millions of people a year, and children suffer the most serious injuries.
why.et: Eating dog is taboo in most of the world, but dog meat is still eaten in some East Asian countries, including China, Vietnam and Korea.

wt: Under 1 kg to about 70 kg, depending on breed
rg: Worldwide, wherever people live. About three-quarters of the world’s dogs are in developing countries, mostly as street and feral dogs.
df: An omnivore. Living alongside people, dogs gained the ability to thrive on a starchy diet that would not suit wolves or other wild dogs.

cf.tip: A wolf has longer legs, bigger feet, a broader head and a straight tail carried low. Many dogs carry their tails curled or high.

src.title: Animal Diversity Web: Canis lupus familiaris
